ex: Con un riverente cenno del capo, il segretario si ritirò dalla sala.
exEn: With a deferential nod, the secretary withdrew from the room.
note: Formal/literary; 'riverente saluto' in ceremonial letters. Cf. 'reverente' (variant, rarer) and 'riverenza' (a bow or curtsey).

ex: Rispose a ogni obiezione con una compitezza che disarmava gli avversari.
exEn: He answered every objection with a politeness that disarmed his opponents.
note: Formal/literary; from 'compìto' (well-mannered). Neutral 'cortesia', 'garbo'.

ex: La buona creanza vuole che l'ospite sia servito per primo.
exEn: Good manners require that the guest be served first.
note: Dated/literary but alive in 'buona creanza' and 'malacreanza' (rudeness); Spanish loan (crianza). 'Educazione' is the neutral word.

ex: Uno screanzato mi è passato davanti in fila senza nemmeno scusarsi.
exEn: A boor pushed in front of me in the queue without even apologising.
note: Colloquial-literary, also used as a noun; from 'creanza'. Synonyms by strength: 'maleducato' (neutral) < 'screanzato' < 'zotico', 'cafone'.

ex: Fu riguardoso verso la vedova e non nominò mai le circostanze dell'incidente.
exEn: He was considerate towards the widow and never mentioned the circumstances of the accident.
note: Formal; 'riguardoso di' or 'verso'. Opposite 'irriguardoso' (disrespectful). Cf. 'premuroso' (attentive, caring).

ex: Provava un timore reverenziale davanti al vecchio maestro.
exEn: He felt a reverential awe in the presence of the old master.
note: Formal; almost always in 'timore reverenziale' (awe), which is also a legal concept invalidating consent obtained through it.

en: I beg your pardon; forgive me
ex: Chiedo venia per il ritardo: il treno è rimasto fermo mezz'ora in galleria.
exEn: Forgive me for the delay: the train sat in a tunnel for half an hour.
note: Formal or mock-formal (often ironic); 'venia' (pardon) is a Latinism used almost only in this phrase. Neutral 'mi scusi'.

ex: Il sugo, con licenza parlando, faceva schifo.
exEn: The sauce, if you'll pardon the expression, was disgusting.
note: Dated courtesy formula that softens a coarse word; regional/colloquial variant 'con rispetto parlando'.

ex: Abbia pazienza, ma quello che dice non corrisponde ai fatti.
exEn: With respect, what you say does not match the facts.
note: Courtesy formula (formal 'Lei' form) that prefaces a disagreement or a request; informal 'abbi pazienza'. Not a literal request for patience.

ex: «Le ho tenuto il posto.» «Obbligatissimo, signora.»
exEn: 'I kept your seat for you.' 'Much obliged, madam.'
note: Dated, ceremonious; now jocular or in period fiction. Absolute superlative of 'obbligato' in the sense 'indebted'.

ex: Le porgo i miei più vivi rallegramenti per la nomina.
exEn: Please accept my warmest congratulations on your appointment.
note: Formal, plural only; 'porgere/esprimere rallegramenti'. Neutral 'congratulazioni', also formal 'felicitazioni'.

ex: Il presidente ha inviato un messaggio augurale alle famiglie dei militari.
exEn: The president sent a message of good wishes to the soldiers' families.
note: Formal/journalistic: 'messaggio augurale', 'brindisi augurale', 'cartoncino augurale'. Not 'augural' in the English sense of omen.

ex: Il discorso si chiuse con parole beneauguranti per il nuovo anno accademico.
exEn: The speech ended with auspicious words for the new academic year.
note: Formal; also spelt 'ben augurante'. Antonym 'malaugurante' or, of omens, 'di malaugurio'.

ex: In attesa di un Suo cortese riscontro, distintamente La saluto.
exEn: Awaiting your kind reply, I remain yours faithfully.
note: Formal letter-closing formula ('distintamente', 'La saluto distintamente'); also the ordinary sense 'clearly, distinctly'.

ex: Alzò il calice di grappa e disse soltanto: «Prosit!»
exEn: He raised his glass of grappa and simply said, 'Cheers!'
note: Latinism ('may it benefit'), heard at toasts, in Alpine regions and, jocularly, after a priest's Mass. Everyday 'cin cin', 'salute'.

ex: Discusse la proposta con l'urbanità di chi non ha bisogno di alzare la voce.
exEn: He discussed the proposal with the urbanity of someone who has no need to raise his voice.
note: Literary; adjective 'urbano' (courteous), antonym 'inurbano'. No connection with cities in this sense except etymology.

ex: I passeggeri furono fatti salire sulle scialuppe di salvataggio in ordine di ponte.
exEn: The passengers were put into the lifeboats deck by deck.
note: Nautical; 'scialuppa di salvataggio'. Cf. 'lancia' (launch), 'zattera' (raft), 'canotto' (dinghy).

ex: Chiusero i boccaporti prima che la tempesta investisse la nave.
exEn: They closed the hatches before the storm hit the ship.
note: Nautical; 'chiudere/serrare i boccaporti' is also used figuratively (batten down the hatches).

ex: Il comandante restò in plancia tutta la notte a scrutare il radar.
exEn: The captain stayed on the bridge all night watching the radar.
note: Nautical ('plancia di comando'); in cars 'plancia' is the dashboard, more technical than 'cruscotto'. Plural 'plance'.

ex: Le gomene si tesero e la nave si staccò lentamente dalla banchina.
exEn: The hawsers went taut and the ship slowly pulled away from the quay.
note: Nautical/literary; thicker than 'cima' (line) or 'cavo'. Dante's 'gomena' in Inferno XXXI.

ex: Due rimorchiatori guidarono la petroliera fuori dal porto.
exEn: Two tugboats guided the tanker out of the harbour.
note: Nautical; from 'rimorchiare' (to tow). 'Rimorchio' is a trailer or the act of towing.

ex: Dalla carlinga il pilota vide le luci della pista comparire tra le nuvole.
exEn: From the cockpit the pilot saw the runway lights appear through the clouds.
note: Aeronautical, slightly dated; modern usage prefers 'cabina di pilotaggio'; 'fusoliera' is the fuselage.

ex: Durante il rullaggio l'aereo si fermò per far passare un'ambulanza.
exEn: During taxiing the plane stopped to let an ambulance pass.
note: Aeronautical; 'pista di rullaggio' = taxiway; verb 'rullare'.

ex: Il postiglione frustò i cavalli e la diligenza ripartì verso Bologna.
exEn: The postilion whipped the horses and the stagecoach set off again for Bologna.
note: Historical/literary; rider or driver of post-horses. Cf. 'cocchiere' (coachman), 'vetturino' (cab driver).

ex: Il vetturino chiese il doppio della tariffa perché pioveva.
exEn: The cab driver asked for twice the fare because it was raining.
note: Dated/literary (nineteenth-century novels); the modern taxi driver is 'tassista'. Also 'fiaccheraio' (Florence).

ex: L'obliteratrice era guasta e il controllore fece una multa a metà vagone.
exEn: The ticket machine was broken and the inspector fined half the carriage.
note: Bureaucratic; 'obliterare il biglietto' = to validate. Everyday 'timbrare', 'convalidare', colloquial 'macchinetta'.

ex: La ferrovia sarda usa uno scartamento ridotto e i treni sono più stretti.
exEn: The Sardinian railway uses a narrow gauge and the trains are narrower.
note: Railway engineering: 'scartamento ordinario/ridotto'. Unrelated to 'scartare' (to discard) in modern use.

ex: Una vecchia mulattiera collega ancora i due villaggi attraverso il valico.
exEn: An old mule track still links the two villages across the pass.
note: Hiking/mountain vocabulary; wider than a 'sentiero', narrower than a 'carrareccia' (cart track). Also adjective 'strada mulattiera'.

ex: Il cuoco di bordo tirò fuori dalla cambusa le ultime scatolette.
exEn: The ship's cook took the last tins out of the storeroom.
note: Nautical; 'cambusiere' = steward in charge of provisions. In Italian usage it is the store, the kitchen itself is 'cucina di bordo'.

ex: La Capitaneria di porto ha vietato la navigazione per le condizioni del mare.
exEn: The harbour master's office banned sailing because of the sea conditions.
note: Administrative/nautical; 'Capitaneria di porto' is the Italian coastguard authority. Capitalised in official names.

ex: Le navi di grossa stazza non possono più entrare nel bacino di San Marco.
exEn: Large-tonnage ships can no longer enter St Mark's basin.
note: Nautical ('stazza lorda'); figurative and jocular 'un uomo di grande stazza' (a big-built man).

en: draught (depth of a vessel below the waterline)
ex: Il porto è troppo basso per navi con un pescaggio superiore a otto metri.
exEn: The harbour is too shallow for ships with a draught of more than eight metres.
note: Nautical, from 'pescare' in the sense 'to sit in the water'; nothing to do with fishing.

ex: La nonna versava la farina a fontana sulla spianatoia e ci rompeva le uova dentro.
exEn: Grandma poured the flour into a well on the pastry board and cracked the eggs into it.
note: Traditional kitchen vocabulary (Emilia, Tuscany); 'tagliere' is the chopping board, 'mattarello' the rolling pin.

ex: Servì la ribollita con un ramaiolo di rame annerito dagli anni.
exEn: He served the ribollita with a copper ladle blackened by the years.
note: Tuscan/regional; standard 'mestolo'. From 'rame' (copper).

ex: Togliete i tortellini dall'acqua con la schiumarola perché non si rompano.
exEn: Lift the tortellini out of the water with a slotted spoon so they do not break.
note: Kitchen tool; also 'schiumaiola'. Named for skimming foam ('schiuma') off broth.

ex: Portò in tavola la zuppiera fumante e tutti tacquero.
exEn: She brought the steaming tureen to the table and everyone fell silent.
note: Tableware; cf. 'salsiera' (gravy boat), 'insalatiera' (salad bowl), 'fruttiera' (fruit bowl).

en: wine counter; serving of drinks by the glass
ex: In quella vecchia mescita si beve vino sfuso a un euro il bicchiere.
exEn: In that old wine bar they serve wine from the barrel at one euro a glass.
note: Trade/regional: 'vino alla mescita' (by the glass). From 'mescere' (to pour), a literary verb.

ex: Finirono la serata in una bettola del porto dove il vino sapeva di tappo.
exEn: They ended the evening in a dive by the harbour where the wine was corked.
note: Pejorative/colloquial; 'osteria' and 'taverna' are neutral or even nostalgic.

ex: Il convitato di pietra della riunione era il bilancio, di cui nessuno osava parlare.
exEn: The elephant in the room at the meeting was the budget, which no one dared mention.
note: Literary; 'il convitato di pietra' (the Stone Guest of Don Giovanni) = a looming, unmentioned presence. Everyday 'invitato', 'commensale'.

ex: L'anfitrione riempiva i bicchieri prima ancora che fossero vuoti.
exEn: The host was refilling the glasses before they were even empty.
note: Literary/jocular, from Molière's Amphitryon; 'padrone di casa' is the neutral term.

ex: Il cachi acerbo era così allappante che non riuscì a finirlo.
exEn: The unripe persimmon was so astringent that she could not finish it.
note: Sensory/wine vocabulary; verb 'allappare' (to set the teeth on edge). Wine-tasting near-synonym 'tannico'.

ex: La lingua salmistrata si serve fredda, tagliata sottile, con la salsa verde.
exEn: Corned tongue is served cold, thinly sliced, with green sauce.
note: Culinary/technical; 'carne salmistrata'. Distinct from 'salato' (salted) and 'affumicato' (smoked).

ex: Le gozzoviglie di carnevale durarono fino all'alba del mercoledì delle ceneri.
exEn: The carnival carousing went on until dawn on Ash Wednesday.
note: Literary, usually plural; verb 'gozzovigliare'. Near-synonyms 'bagordi', 'baldoria' (neutral), 'crapula' (gluttonous excess).

ex: Gli assediati morivano di inedia mentre i granai nemici traboccavano.
exEn: The besieged were dying of starvation while the enemy granaries overflowed.
note: Literary/medical; 'morire d'inedia'. Neutral 'fame'; 'digiuno' is voluntary fasting.

ex: Satolli e un po' brilli, gli ospiti si trascinarono verso il divano.
exEn: Full up and slightly tipsy, the guests dragged themselves to the sofa.
note: Literary/jocular; neutral 'sazio'. Verb 'satollarsi'. Cf. 'pasciuto' (well-fed).

ex: Le olive vanno tenute in salamoia per almeno un mese prima di essere mangiate.
exEn: The olives must be kept in brine for at least a month before being eaten.
note: Culinary/food-preserving; 'in salamoia' vs 'sott'olio', 'sott'aceto'. Figurative 'tenere in salamoia' (leave hanging) is rare.

ex: Hanno riempito l'intercapedine del muro con materiale isolante per ridurre la dispersione di calore.
exEn: They filled the cavity in the wall with insulating material to reduce heat loss.
note: Building/technical; also figurative in learned prose ('un'intercapedine tra due epoche').

ex: Abbattendo il tramezzo tra cucina e soggiorno hanno ottenuto un unico ambiente luminoso.
exEn: By knocking down the partition wall between kitchen and living room they got a single bright space.
note: Building; non-load-bearing, unlike a 'muro portante'. Variant 'tramezza'. Not to be confused with 'tramezzino' (sandwich).

ex: Il gatto camminava sul cornicione del quarto piano senza alcuna paura.
exEn: The cat walked along the fourth-floor ledge without any fear.
note: Architectural; in Naples 'cornicione' is also the raised rim of a pizza. Cf. 'cornice' (frame).

ex: La porta uscì dai gangheri e restò appesa a una sola cerniera.
exEn: The door came off its hinges and hung from a single one.
note: Technical/dated; alive above all in the idiom 'uscire dai gangheri' (to fly off the handle). Everyday 'cardine', 'cerniera'.

ex: Il pastore si stese sul giaciglio di paglia e si addormentò subito.
exEn: The shepherd lay down on the straw pallet and fell asleep at once.
note: Literary; implies poverty or improvisation ('un misero giaciglio'). Cf. 'pagliericcio' (straw mattress), 'letto' (neutral).

ex: Una spessa coltre di neve copriva i tetti del paese.
exEn: A thick blanket of snow covered the roofs of the village.
note: Literary; the household sense (quilt) survives mainly in the South; the figurative 'coltre di nebbia/silenzio' is common in prose.

ex: I figli accorsero al capezzale del padre morente.
exEn: The children rushed to their dying father's bedside.
note: Formal/literary; 'al capezzale di' (at the bedside of a sick person). Originally the bolster at the bed's head.

en: lye; washing solution made from wood ash
ex: Le lavandaie facevano bollire le lenzuola nella liscivia prima di batterle al fiume.
exEn: The washerwomen boiled the sheets in lye before beating them at the river.
note: Historical/rural; also 'lisciva' and Tuscan 'ranno'. Chemical sense: solution of sodium/potassium hydroxide.

ex: Alla luce della lucerna il notaio copiava l'atto in bella grafia.
exEn: By the light of the oil lamp the notary was copying out the deed in fine handwriting.
note: Historical/literary; the Roman clay lamp and the later brass 'lucerna fiorentina'. Also the carabinieri's cocked hat.

en: fellow tenant; neighbour in the same building
ex: I casigliani si riunirono nell'androne per protestare contro il rumore.
exEn: The tenants of the building gathered in the entrance hall to protest about the noise.
note: Regional (Rome, Naples) and dated; standard 'condomino', 'vicino di casa'. Also 'casigliano' as adjective.

en: neighbour opposite; person living across the way
ex: La dirimpettaia spiava dal balcone tutto ciò che succedeva nel cortile.
exEn: The woman across the way spied from her balcony on everything that happened in the courtyard.
note: Colloquial-literary, from 'dirimpetto' (opposite); no neutral one-word equivalent.

ex: Vivevano in sei in un tugurio senza finestre, con il tetto che perdeva.
exEn: Six of them lived in a windowless hovel with a leaking roof.
note: Literary, strongly pejorative. Near-synonyms: 'catapecchia' (ramshackle hut), 'stamberga' (dingy dump), 'topaia' (rat hole).

ex: Il conte ricevette gli ospiti nell'antica magione di famiglia.
exEn: The count received his guests in the ancient family mansion.
note: Literary, often ironic or jocular today ('la mia umile magione'); Gallicism (maison). Neutral 'dimora', 'villa'.

ex: Lo studio legale occupa l'ammezzato tra il pianterreno e il primo piano.
exEn: The law firm occupies the mezzanine between the ground floor and the first floor.
note: Architectural/estate-agent vocabulary; synonym 'mezzanino'. Typical of nineteenth-century Italian palazzi.

en: small fry; odds and ends; trivial details
ex: Il cassetto era pieno di minutaglia: bottoni, chiavi, tappi e ricevute.
exEn: The drawer was full of odds and ends: buttons, keys, corks and receipts.
note: Colloquial-literary, slightly dismissive; also of small fish or unimportant people. Cf. 'minuzia' (a trifle), 'cianfrusaglie'.

ex: I lavori stradali sono un intralcio continuo alla circolazione del quartiere.
exEn: The roadworks are a constant hindrance to traffic in the neighbourhood.
note: Formal; 'essere d'intralcio a', 'intralcio alla giustizia' (obstruction of justice, legal). Cf. 'intoppo' (snag), 'impiccio' (nuisance).

ex: La sua pignoleria nel controllare ogni scontrino esasperava i colleghi.
exEn: His fussiness in checking every receipt exasperated his colleagues.
note: Colloquial, mildly pejorative; from 'pignolo'. Positive equivalents 'meticolosità', 'scrupolo'; near-synonym 'pedanteria' (of scholars).

ex: Le operaie lavoravano alacri per finire la commessa prima di Natale.
exEn: The women worked briskly to finish the order before Christmas.
note: Literary; noun 'alacrità', adverb 'alacremente'. Latinism (alacer); stress on the first syllable: àlacre.

ex: La trovai affaccendata tra i fornelli, con tre pentole sul fuoco.
exEn: I found her bustling about at the stove, with three pots on the go.
note: Literary-colloquial; from 'faccenda'. Cf. 'indaffarato' (neutral), 'occupato' (plain).

ex: Un gruppo di giovani sfaccendati passava le giornate sulla panchina della piazza.
exEn: A group of idle youths spent their days on the bench in the square.
note: Mildly pejorative, also a noun ('uno sfaccendato'). Register between 'disoccupato' (neutral) and 'fannullone', 'scioperato' (harsher).

ex: I nottambuli del centro si ritrovano al chiosco del cornetto caldo alle quattro del mattino.
exEn: The city-centre night owls meet at the hot-croissant kiosk at four in the morning.
note: Also adjective; formed on the model of 'sonnambulo' (sleepwalker). Opposite 'mattiniero' (early riser).

ex: Dopo la carbonara mi è venuto un abbiocco tremendo e ho dormito un'ora.
exEn: After the carbonara I was hit by a terrible drowsiness and slept for an hour.
note: Colloquial, originally Roman, now nationwide; 'avere/venire l'abbiocco', verb 'abbioccarsi'. Neutral 'sonnolenza'.

ex: Il caldo del pomeriggio immerse la casa in un sopore dal quale nessuno voleva uscire.
exEn: The afternoon heat plunged the house into a drowsiness no one wanted to leave.
note: Literary/medical ('stato soporoso'); Latinism (sopor). Everyday 'sonnolenza', figurative 'torpore'.

ex: Ha comprato un aggeggio che dovrebbe sbucciare le mele da solo.
exEn: He bought a contraption that is supposed to peel apples by itself.
note: Colloquial, slightly dismissive; near-synonyms 'marchingegno' (complicated device), 'arnese' (tool), 'coso' (thingummy).

ex: Sotto il frigorifero c'era un sudiciume di anni.
exEn: Under the fridge there was years' worth of grime.
note: Pejorative; adjective 'sudicio'. Stronger than 'sporcizia'; 'luridume', 'lordura' are literary equivalents.

ex: La cucina era linda e profumava di limone.
exEn: The kitchen was spotless and smelt of lemon.
note: Literary-colloquial, often in 'lindo e pinto' (neat as a pin). Neutral 'pulito'; 'terso' is used of air, sky and glass.

ex: Dopo il temporale il cielo era terso e si vedevano le Alpi.
exEn: After the storm the sky was clear and you could see the Alps.
note: Literary; of sky, air, glass and, figuratively, of prose style ('una prosa tersa'). From 'tergere' (to wipe).

ex: La collazione dei tre manoscritti ha rivelato una lacuna comune a due di essi.
exEn: Collating the three manuscripts revealed a gap common to two of them.
note: Philology; verb 'collazionare'. In law 'collazione' is the return of gifts to the estate before division among heirs.

en: stemma (family tree of manuscripts); coat of arms
ex: Lo stemma codicum ricostruito dall'editore fa risalire tutte le copie a un unico archetipo.
exEn: The stemma reconstructed by the editor traces all the copies back to a single archetype.
note: Philology (Lachmann's method) and heraldry; masculine despite the -a ending, plural 'stemmi'.

en: colophon (printer's note at the end of a book)
ex: Il colophon indica che il volume fu finito di stampare a Venezia nel 1499.
exEn: The colophon states that the volume was finished printing in Venice in 1499.
note: Bibliography/publishing; Greek loan, invariable, stress on the first syllable. Modern books put it on the copyright page.

ex: Ogni capitolo si apre con un capolettera miniato in oro e azzurro.
exEn: Each chapter opens with an initial illuminated in gold and blue.
note: Manuscript studies and typography; irregular plural 'capilettera'. Cf. 'iniziale'.

ex: Mia nonna imparò a leggere su un sillabario del ventennio con le figure dei balilla.
exEn: My grandmother learnt to read from a Fascist-era primer with pictures of the Balilla boys.
note: Historical (pre-1970s schooling); the earlier 'abbecedario' taught letters, the 'sillabario' syllables and words.

ex: Il giovane principe ebbe come precettore un abate esperto di greco.
exEn: The young prince had as his tutor an abbot expert in Greek.
note: Historical/literary; the tutor lived in the household. Cf. 'istitutore' (same, nineteenth century), modern 'insegnante privato'.

en: docimology (the science of assessment and testing)
ex: Secondo la docimologia, un voto senza criteri espliciti misura più l'esaminatore che l'esaminato.
exEn: According to docimology, a mark without explicit criteria measures the examiner more than the examinee.
note: Educational-science jargon, standard in Italian teacher-training; adjective 'docimologico'.

ex: Nell'Italia del 1861 la gran parte della popolazione era illetterata.
exEn: In the Italy of 1861 most of the population was unlettered.
note: Formal; also noun. 'Analfabeta' = cannot read or write; 'illetterato' = without literary education; 'incolto' = uncultured.

ex: La nuova didattica mette il discente, e non il docente, al centro del processo.
exEn: The new teaching approach puts the learner, not the teacher, at the centre of the process.
note: Educational-science jargon, paired with 'docente'; Latinism (discens). Everyday 'studente', 'allievo'.

ex: «A me mi piace» è il solecismo più citato dalle grammatiche scolastiche.
exEn: 'A me mi piace' is the solecism most often cited by school grammars.
note: Learned; a syntactic error, whereas 'barbarismo' is a wrongly formed word and 'strafalcione' any gross blunder.

ex: Dire «qual'è» con l'apostrofo è un errore, ma scrivere «un'altro» è un ipercorrettismo di segno opposto.
exEn: Saying 'qual'è' with an apostrophe is a mistake, but writing 'un'altro' is a hypercorrection in the opposite direction.
note: Linguistics; also 'ipercorrezione'. Typical of speakers over-applying a rule they have learnt late.

ex: «Traduttore, traditore» è la paronomasia più celebre della lingua italiana.
exEn: 'Traduttore, traditore' is the most famous paronomasia in the Italian language.
note: Rhetoric; everyday 'gioco di parole', 'bisticcio'. Also 'annominazione'.
